messages.author: 10c8cda73c65d9b2
messages.subject: Flexibility to Access Base Functions
parts:
Great product!  Your package eliminates the hurdles in importing xlsx files.

I would like to know how to access the base functions your code uses so that we can use this package to make the most use out of it.  For example, the documentation does not have an example of how to retrieve sheet names in an Excel file, but in looking through the function I have found that it can be accomplished by using wb$getNumberOfSheets() and wb$getSheetName.  Is there a place I can look to get an exhaustive list of these functions?

messages.author: 1db601ea1fed90a0
messages.subject: Re: Flexibility to Access Base Functions
parts:
In the examples for the ?Workbook


# see all the available java methods that you can call
.jmethods(wb)


>  wb
[1] "Java-Object{Name: /xl/workbook.xml - Content Type: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet.main+xml}"

In general, you can do this on all the Java Objects.  Sometimes, the R objects are a wrapper around the Java Object.  For example, 
for CellBlock:

>    cb <- CellBlock(sheet, 1, 1, 3, 3, create = TRUE)   
> cb
$ref
[1] "Java-Object{org.cran.rexcel.RCellBlock@4c4cd88f}"

attr(,"class")
[1] "CellBlock"
> 
you will have to do .jmethods(cb$ref).  

The best way to understand the result of .jmethods is to look at the POI official javadocs.

http://poi.apache.org/apidocs/index.html

for example an xlsx workbook is an instance of class org.apache.poi.xssf.usermodel.XSSFWorkbook so you check out 
http://poi.apache.org/apidocs/org/apache/poi/xssf/usermodel/XSSFWorkbook.html

Adrian
